items.title: PCRS and NHS Wales primary care respiratory update, Cardiff, 20 October 2026
items.summary: PCRS is running a one-day essential primary care respiratory update in Cardiff on Tuesday 20 October 2026, with NHS Wales Performance and Improvement and members of the National Respiratory Audit Programme. A concentrated Welsh primary care respiratory audience.

items.title: PCRS webinar on breathlessness and chronic cough in adults, 30 September
items.summary: PCRS emailed members on 14 August 2026 announcing a webinar, Breathlessness and chronic cough in adults: challenges currently being faced by primary care, on Wednesday 30 September 2026, 19:00 to 20:00. Date and time taken from the PCRS mailing; not yet confirmed on the public PCRS events listing.

items.title: Prime Minister issues apology to social care nurses for ‘being let down for so long’
items.summary: The Prime Minister has assured nurses and other professionals working in social care they are ‘not invisible’ to his government and has apologised for the way in which they have been ‘let down’ by politicians.

items.title: Proposed national care service ‘utterly essential’ to securing NHS future, says Burnham
items.summary: The Prime Minister has used his speech at the Labour Party conference to warn that a broken social care ‘will break the NHS too’.

items.title: ‘I’m not an anxious person, but general practice has pushed me to my limits’
items.summary: Dr Katie Musgrave opens up about the work-induced anxiety she has experienced in general practice, wondering if others are suffering in silence Has anybody else ever experienced that heart-sinking feeling when you’re due to go back to work after a holiday, and you just can’t face it?

items.title: ‘I wasn’t emotionally prepared for retiring from being a GP’
items.summary: Former GP Mary Coyne shares her experience of how the emotional impact of retiring caught her by surprise As I started to approach retirement, I began to wonder what it might look like. The standard definition of ‘leaving your job and stopping work’ was not to my liking.

items.title: BMA opposes Government plans for trusts to commission primary care
items.summary: The BMA has opposed plans for trusts to commission primary care as part of the neighbourhood health model.

items.title: New ‘workplace health system’ to prevent GP fit notes
items.summary: The Government is pushing ahead with its plan to create a ‘workplace health system’ to help people stay in work and prevent the need for GP fit notes.

items.title: NMC four-year midwifery strategy targets racism and safety
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) has set out a four-year strategy for midwifery regulation aimed at supporting safer maternity care, with equity and anti-racism among its listed priorities.

items.title: RCN president warns immigration reforms could destabilise social care
items.summary: Royal College of Nursing (RCN) president Bejoy Sebastian has renewed calls for the home secretary to scrap proposed immigration reforms for care workers, arguing they are incompatible with ambitions for a national care service and could further destabilise social care.

items.title: AP concerns ‘similar’ to those around physician associates, says BMA
items.summary: The BMA has demanded an ‘urgent review’ is launched by the Government into the scopes of practice for advanced practitioners.

items.title: Nurses caught ‘snooping’ on patient records will be suspended immediately, warns NHSE
items.summary: Nurses and health professionals suspected of accessing patient records ‘improperly and unlawfully’ will be suspended immediately, NHS England (NHSE) has warned.

items.title: Health visitors win job evaluation after industrial action
items.summary: Health visitors employed by NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde (NHS GCC) have halted industrial action after the health board agreed to complete a job evaluation process.

items.title: PM pledges to put NHS-style care service plans before electorate
items.summary: Plans for an NHS-style national care service, free at the point of delivery, will be in the Labour manifesto ahead of the next general election, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged. In a BBC interview, Mr Burnham warned that ‘broken social care will break the National Health Service if we leave it like it is’...

items.title: ‘When GPs think they know the whole story’
items.summary: Runner-up in our writing competition, Dr LM explores the danger of believing that GPs can understand a patient’s life from a single consultation, and the assumptions that quietly fill in the gaps The lie I tell my patients is that I understand. I nod at the right moments.

items.title: Persistent ketoacidosis risk found with SGLT2 diabetes drugs
items.summary: Patients taking widely used SGLT2 inhibitor drugs for type 2 diabetes can remain at risk of ketoacidosis throughout treatment, a large Scandinavian study suggests. Ketoacidosis is a potentially life-threatening complication caused by a build-up of ketones in the blood.

items.title: NHS England instructs GP practices to dismiss staff caught ‘snooping’ on patient records
items.summary: GP practices should sack employees caught ‘snooping’ patient records ‘in almost all cases’, according to NHS England.

items.title: Implementing Benedict’s law: guidance from a school nurse
items.summary: Following the launch of new statutory allergy safety guidance this month, all state-maintained schools, academies and free schools are expected to meet a number of requirements relating to staff allergy training and allergy safety policies, among other things.

items.title: A quicker way to work through patient symptoms
items.summary: Tiredness. Calf pain. A persistent cough. An unfamiliar rash. In primary care, a seemingly straightforward symptom can have a long list of possible causes. Nursing in Practice Reference is designed to help nurses work through them.

items.title: Semaglutide linked to 40% reduction in asthma attacks
items.summary: Weight loss and diabetes treatment semaglutide is associated with a nearly 40% reduction in asthma attacks among people with the condition, according to new analysis.

items.title: Hospitals paid up to ten times more than GPs to monitor adult ADHD patients, LMC claims
items.summary: Exclusive GP leaders in one area have claimed they have been offered ten times less than hospitals to deliver the same ADHD service.

items.title: Children as young as 13 seen by NHS for bladder damage caused by ketamine
items.summary: Children as young as 13 for bladder problems associated with ketamine use according to doctors who set up an NHS clinic to manage the problem.

items.title: Panel sides with Operose as ICB ‘breached regulations’ when awarding GP contracts
items.summary: An independent panel has sided with Operose as it found one ICB has breached regulations during contract awards for two London GP practices.

items.title: Can GPs win the fight for funding this time?
items.summary: Pulse editor Sofia Lind asks whether GPs can use the threat of industrial action to win greater control over their funding This week the BMA issued a stark warning about the NHS’s increasing reliance on non-doctors, with some seriously frightening examples of patient safety being put at risk.

items.title: Quick cases in gastroenterology
items.summary: Our latest CPD module explores five clinical scenarios in gastroenterology, covering ulcerative colitis flare, coeliac disease monitoring, persistent dyspepsia, chronic diarrhoea with a negative FIT result and interpreting liver scan findings. Complete the full module on Pulse 365 today.

items.title: Hospital signs lease for GP facilities in move towards providing neighbourhood services
items.summary: A hospital group said that it has ‘helped secure the future’ of a GP practice by signing a five-year lease agreement for its facilities, with a view to provide neighbourhood services in the future.

items.title: Current approach to detecting and treating hypertension is not working, say researchers
items.summary: The current approach to detecting and treating hypertension is ‘not fit for purpose’ say researchers who found high levels of undiagnosed and uncontrolled disease across the country.

items.title: More nurses needed in primary care to meet vaccination demand, conference hears
items.summary: Primary care services require more nurses to help meet expanding vaccination schedules and to ensure enough appointments are available, a Nursing in Practice conference has heard.

items.title: Minister reiterates nurse pay is up to GP practices to decide
items.summary: The new minister responsible for general practice has recognised that GP contractual arrangements ‘do not place any specific obligations’ on practices when it comes to nurse terms and conditions.

items.title: ‘As budgets get squished, so do school nursing teams’
items.summary: Professional officer and clinical school nurse lead Susie Scale has shared the diverse roles of school nurses – highlighting it as one of the very few roles to work between health, education and social care.

items.title: Patient safety alert issued to prevent avoidable harm from hoists
items.summary: Health and care organisations have been told to take a series of ‘urgent and practical steps’ to reduce avoidable harms when using patient hoists.

items.title: Practices struggling to stay open due to ‘severe’ nursing shortages
items.summary: GP practices in Wales are struggling to stay open amid a ‘severe shortage’ of nurses and other primary care colleagues, a new report has warned.

items.title: Polymyalgia rheumatica – when to suspect and how to test for it
items.summary: Under the radar: GPSI in MSK medicine Dr Louise Warburton describes how polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) symptoms can be misattributed – in this case to work stress and worsening osteoarthritis – and explains how symptoms and signs can be recognised and investigated promptly Note the case in this article is hypothetical…

items.title: GPs should let parents access children’s records but keep this ‘under review’, says GMC
items.summary: GPs should let parents access their child’s medical records if the child consents, but they should keep this decision ‘under review’, the GMC has said in new draft guidance.
